title: Second-hand first: the two-minute check before buying new

body.heading: What second-hand suits best
paragraphs: Some categories are second-hand gold: furniture, textbooks, sports equipment, children's clothes, tools, and board games. These are durable things people sell because they moved, grew, or lost interest — not because the item failed.
Electronics need more care: check the battery health, the charger, and whether the model still receives updates. A short checklist turns a gamble into a judgement.

body.heading: The two-minute routine
paragraphs: Before buying new, spend two minutes searching a local marketplace or charity shop listing. If a good used version exists at half price or less, you have saved real money for two minutes of effort — a very respectable hourly rate.
If nothing turns up, buy new with a clear conscience. The check is the habit; it does not have to succeed every time to pay for itself across a year.

body.heading: Safety and sense
paragraphs: Meet sellers in public places, pay through traceable methods for larger items, and test before you pay when you can. For safety equipment — helmets, car seats, smoke alarms — new is usually the wiser buy, because hidden damage matters.
Buying second-hand is also quietly good for the planet: every used item bought is one less new item manufactured and one less thing landfilled. Thrift and thoughtfulness point the same way here.

takeaway: Make "check second-hand first" a two-minute reflex for durable goods, and let new be the deliberate exception rather than the default.
